title: A-Eye system map
measured_note: Measured on real Gemini Live calls with synthetic speech (latest runs, 2026-10-25). Anything else says not measured.
cost_note: Costs are provider list prices, estimates from the price pages. Local models cost $0 cloud. Our safety meter counts high on purpose; its figures are in the Cost panel.

nodes.name: Camera + mic
nodes.what: The phone or browser streams microphone audio and one camera frame per second, downscaled to 320 px, over one WebSocket. It plays the voice reply and draws boxes on the live view.

nodes.name: A-Eye server /ws2
nodes.what: One socket per call. It fans each turn out to the router, the safety gates, the step guide, vision and memory, and relays Gemini's voice back. Code decides what is safe and which step is next; models only phrase and look.

nodes.name: Gemini Live talker
nodes.what: Hears the voice and sees 1 fps frames, then speaks. It is the only voice in the normal call. The session resumes after a provider goAway or drop, with up to 3 quiet retries (0.5, 1 and 2 s). Safety gates can mute it mid sentence and speak a fixed line instead.
facts: End of speech to first voice
$0.016 / min (mic + 1 fps video, 50/50 talk) to $0.025 / min (full duplex), estimate
our safety meter (counts high on purpose)
$0.10 / connection-minute (GEMINI_LIVE_USD_PER_MINUTE), billed at connect and every 60 s, idle included
resumes with a session handle on goAway or drop; up to 3 quiet retries at 0.5, 1 and 2 s (RECONNECT_DELAYS); slidingWindow keeps context

look.title: Measured response times
look.foot: Measured on real Live calls, 2026-10-25, synthetic speech. Prices: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (page 2026-10-22).

nodes.name: Decision model
nodes.kind: Router and time-scope decision model in front of memory (EmbeddingGemma + logistic regression)
nodes.what: Embeds each question and picks a lane: answer from now (camera), from memory, or ask the expert. A time-scope head then picks how far back: seconds, minutes, earlier this call or earlier calls. A past question holds Gemini's reply until code has looked it up. Local, about 45 ms on CPU.
facts: 91% of 300 questions, 0 "now" questions held by mistake (independent set, team report)

look.title: Router vs alternatives, 100 held-out questions
look.foot: Lane accuracy from router/results/heldout_eval.json. Time scope: 91% on an independent 300-question set, 0 "now" held by mistake; 93 of 100 on the repo held-out set.

nodes.name: Safety gates
nodes.what: Plain code, no model. A question about a known hazard gets a fixed line and no model is asked; a reply that calls a hazard fine is replaced. Touching the hot soldering iron tip, wiring with USB plugged in, or mains power each get a fixed line. On a hazard it mutes Gemini and speaks the stop line 86 ms after speech ends.
facts: "Do not touch the hot soldering iron tip; leave it in its stand." / "Unplug the USB first."
the model never decides what is safe; fixed lines are spoken by code
a context note cannot fire a gate on low-voltage work (headphones, USB, Arduino); only an explicit current hazard reaches the gates (server/context_agent.py)

look.title: After the user stops speaking
look.foot: The gate speaks first, so the model never gets to say the unsafe thing.

nodes.name: Step guide
nodes.what: Code owns the task and the current step; Gemini only phrases it. Coded tasks: the Arduino LED build, resistor bands, LED polarity, a multimeter resistance check and tying a four-in-hand tie. Every wiring step starts with USB unplugged. A step moves only when the guide's rules pass on what the son says.
facts: LED build 7, resistor bands 2, LED polarity 2, multimeter 6, tie 8 steps
"Unplug the USB first" before wiring; a 220 ohm resistor in series before USB
never measure resistance on a powered circuit; black to COM, red to V or ohms, never A or mA
mains power and wall outlets get a fixed stop line

look.title: What the son can learn (coded on main)

cards.head: Arduino LED build, 7 steps
cards.body: Parts, LED rows, 220 ohm to GND, pin 9, GND, USB, Blink upload.

cards.head: Resistor bands, 2 steps
cards.body: Read from the end opposite the tolerance band; red red brown is 220 ohms.

cards.head: LED polarity, 2 steps
cards.body: Long leg is plus, flat rim is minus.

cards.head: Multimeter, 6 steps
cards.body: Power off, probes to COM and V/ohms, ohm range, measure the loose resistor, read, turn off.

cards.head: Tie a tie, 8 steps
cards.body: Four-in-hand: drape, cross, wrap, cross, up through the loop, down through the band, dimple, slide up.

cards.head: Soldering
cards.body: Hot-iron safety gate only; no coded steps.

nodes.building: Soldering has the hot-iron safety gate and a part card, but no coded steps.

nodes.name: Context builder
nodes.what: Every ~4 seconds in the background it writes a short scene note from the transcript and recent frames and hands it to Gemini, so answers know what happened. With Claude switched off it falls back to a local model.
facts: one note every 4 s, 15 per minute, max_tokens 320
about 1,500 in + 100 out per note, estimate
our safety meter (counts high on purpose)

nodes.name: Grounding boxes
nodes.what: When you name an object it finds it in the frame and returns a box, drawn on your screen about 2 s after the object is named. If the home GPU is unavailable and cloud fallback is set, Gemini vision answers instead.
facts: serial GPU: about 0.5 boxes / s, estimate
about 1 concurrent pointer user at demo quality
Tailscale only; frames stay on our GPU
Gemini cloud vision when VISION_BACKEND=cloud_fallback and the Google switch is on (server/cloud_vision.py)

look.title: Object named to box on screen

nodes.name: Captions
nodes.what: Writes short captions of frames so recent memory can answer "what did I just do?".
facts: Gemini cloud vision when VISION_BACKEND=cloud_fallback and the Google switch is on (server/cloud_vision.py)

nodes.name: YOLO detector
nodes.what: Fast object detection on frames, served by boxsvc on the GPU box, bound to the tailnet only.

nodes.name: Guest / local mode
nodes.kind: Whisper + Kokoro (boxsvc) + local brain + local vision
nodes.what: Guest / local mode turns every cloud switch off. Whisper turns speech into text, a local model answers, local vision finds parts, and Kokoro speaks, all on our own machines. $0 cloud.
facts: first audio 0.060 s on the box, measured
Whole call as a Live replacement
$0 cloud; home GPU electricity about $0.0007 / session-minute, estimate
weaker talker (local 3.75 vs Haiku 4.81 on a 16-image set, measured), no Rewind, no Live barge-in

nodes.name: Recent memory
nodes.what: Keeps notes of what was said and seen for the last 10 minutes so "what did I just do?" is answered from text. A question about up to 5 minutes ago reads these notes; older goes to Rewind.
facts: 10 minutes of notes in RAM (KEEP_S 600), cleared on hang-up
questions about up to 5 minutes ago (RECENT_MAX_S 300); older goes to Rewind

nodes.what: With memory consent, a call is saved, encrypted on disk when the memory key is set. In open demo mode every call is kept for the team library. Questions about earlier calls go through the decision model to a TwelveLabs search of kept clips first; the clip plays in the card as an MP4.
facts: 0.483 ms median local file lookup, measured (fixture)

nodes.name: Planning team
nodes.what: For a task with no coded guide, one Claude Haiku 5.5 call with a forced submit_plan tool writes up to 8 steps. A code safety checker replaces unsafe steps with calm precautions, then code runs the plan like a coded guide ("Guide: plan 1/6") while Gemini handles the first reply.
facts: about 4 to 6 s, measured in real calls
2 to 8, each with say, show and safety
15 of 15 bad plans caught; 1 of 13 good plans wrongly dropped

flows.name: Ask a question
flows.say: Voice and frames reach the server, the router picks a lane in about 45 ms, Gemini answers with the latest scene note. First voice 0.5 to 1.4 s after you stop.

detail.path: Phone 1 fps 320 px frames + audio to /ws2 on the Mac, to Gemini Live in the cloud. The router (about 45 ms, local) picks now, memory or expert; the Haiku context builder adds a scene note every ~4 s; safety gates run in code before playback.
detail.out: Mic audio and downscaled frames to Google. With Claude on: question text, scene note, last dialogue, sometimes one crop.
detail.latency: End of speech to first voice 0.5 to 1.4 s, measured. Router 45.7 ms p50, measured. Time to write one note not measured.
detail.cost: Gemini list $0.016 to $0.025 / min; Haiku notes $0.003 / min, estimate.
detail.runs: Until hang-up; the Gemini connection resumes about every 10 min.

flows.name: Find an object
flows.say: "Where is it?" routes to grounding on the home GPU; the box is on your screen about 2 s after you name it.

detail.path: Named object to pointer grounding: Qwen 3.5 9B on the home GPU over Tailscale; YOLO can pre-detect; the box is drawn on the live view.
detail.out: None for the box; frames stay on our GPU (Live still has its own audio and frames).
detail.latency: Object named to box on screen about 2 s, measured.
detail.runs: One grounding call; about 0.5 boxes / s on one GPU, estimate.

flows.name: Hazard stop
flows.say: "Can I touch the iron tip?" A coded gate catches it, mutes Gemini and plays the stop line 86 ms after you stop speaking.

detail.path: Speech to /ws2 to server/safety.py and the pack refuse() check, in code. On a hit Gemini is muted and the fixed line is spoken; no model is asked that turn.
detail.out: The hazard turn is not answered by Claude or Live.
detail.latency: Stop line 86 ms after speech, Gemini muted, measured.
detail.cost: $0 for the gate (the Live minute still bills while open).
detail.runs: One spoken stop; the call can continue.

flows.name: Rewind
flows.say: "Where did I leave the multimeter?" The decision model sends it to a TwelveLabs visual search (object words, best of the top 5) and the clip plays in the card.

detail.path: Scene-change cuts (2 s pre-roll + 3 to 12 s) become in-memory MP4 clips sent to TwelveLabs; "what did I do earlier?" goes through the router's time scope to a Rewind search.
detail.out: Silent clips to TwelveLabs; on by default in this demo, off with the Rewind button; deleted at call end unless kept.
detail.latency: Searchable 35 to 40 s after the event, measured on the 60 s flush; 11 to 20 s with flush 0, estimate. Search 0.3 to 1.1 s, measured.
detail.cost: Busy minute about $0.033 at list, estimate.
detail.runs: While Rewind is on for the call.

flows.name: Plan a new task
flows.say: "The wire on my headphones broke, how do I fix it?" Gemini answers first; Haiku writes up to 8 steps in about 4 to 6 s; code checks every step and runs the plan.

detail.path: Camera and mic to /ws2, router finds no coded guide, one Claude Haiku 5.5 submit_plan call writes the plan, the code safety checker rewrites unsafe steps, the step guide runs it while Gemini phrases each step.
detail.out: The task text to Claude (Claude switch on); voice and frames to Google as in any Live call.
detail.latency: Plan in about 4 to 6 s, measured in real calls; Gemini's first reply is not held.
detail.cost: One Haiku call per plan; cost not measured.
detail.runs: Until the last plan step or the son stops.

flows.name: Guest / local
flows.say: Guest / local: local vision, Whisper, a local brain and Kokoro on our own machines. Nothing leaves home; $0 cloud.

detail.path: Guest sign-in or Private turns Google, Claude, TwelveLabs and Cartesia off. Camera to local Qwen vision, mic to Whisper, a local brain, Kokoro voice. Safety, steps, recent memory and parts stay on.
detail.latency: First voice about 1.0 s, measured (latest acceptance run).
detail.runs: Guest: 24 h cookie, 10 turns / min, 100 admitted actions.

headline.say: A-Eye lets a dad guide his son through fixing and learning electronics, and tying a tie: it sees through the phone camera, talks each step, and coded gates stop it at a hot soldering iron or live USB.

chips.text: about $0.05 to $0.07 per 2.5 min call ($0.13 to $0.15 with Recall), list price, est.

call_cost.title: Cost of one 2.5 min call
call_cost.note: List price, estimate, from the team numbers sheet and the provider price pages.
meter: Our safety meter (counts high on purpose)

One 2.5 min Live call with Rewind measured about $1.40 on it. It bills Gemini at $0.10 per connection-minute, Haiku by budget weights and TwelveLabs at $0.10 per request including free status polls, so the daily cap trips early rather than late.
